newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T up on lawsuit hopes, Morris results.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T up on lawsuit hopes, Morris results.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc rose in late trading on Wednesday, extending earlier gains on fresh hopes of a settlement in U.S. legal claims and after strong first-quarter results from Philip Morris Cos.
B.A.T shares were up 23-1/2p at 536-1/2 by 1451 GMT in active trade of 7.6 million shares, while Morris rose $2-5/8 to $41-1/2 in New York.

Ian Rennardson, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said the Philip Morris figures had given B.A.T shares fresh impetus, after earlier reports that tobacco industry executives were in talks with plaintiffs lawyers on a possible settlement of U.S. litigation against the industry.
"The Morris results were very good and have given a shot to B.A.T shares," Rennardson said, adding that a settlement of U.S. litigation would also be positive for the UK stock.
"Obviously people on all sides want to get the situation sorted out," Rennardson said. "The market hates uncertainty, once it can quantify the situation it will be able to put a price on it."
A source close to the talks told Reuters in the U.S. that the talks had begun two weeks ago and that lawyers hoped the first round would conclude later on Wednesday.
Earlier a spokesman for B.A.T repeated the company's official line that it was ready to consider a settlement. "We will evaluate any sensible proposals made in good faith," the spokesman said.
By 1512 GMT B.A.T shares were up 28p at 541.
